name: Keyboard
explanation: Every action a user can take with a mouse must also be possible using only a keyboard. This covers clicking buttons and links, opening menus, filling in forms, dragging sliders, and dismissing dialogs. It does not mean every interaction has to feel identical to a mouse — a drag-and-drop reorder tool might use arrow keys to move an item up and down the list instead of literally dragging. The one narrow exception is for functions that inherently depend on the path of a gesture, like freehand drawing, where the endpoints alone don't capture what the user did.
whoItAffects: People who can't use a mouse at all — due to a motor disability, a temporary injury, or a broken trackpad — rely entirely on a keyboard, switch device, or voice-control software that emulates key presses. Screen reader users typically navigate by keyboard even if they're also sighted, since a screen reader tracks a virtual cursor rather than a mouse pointer. If any control only responds to a click, hover, or drag, these users hit a hard wall: not a workaround, but total inability to complete that task.
howToTest: Unplug your mouse, or just don't touch it, and try to complete every task on the page using only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and arrow keys. Can you reach every button, link, form field, and custom widget? Can you open menus, select options, and submit forms? Pay special attention to custom-built controls like dropdowns, sliders, date pickers, and drag-and-drop interfaces — these are the most likely to have been wired up for mouse events only and skipped for keyboard entirely.

check.question: A custom-built star rating widget lets users click a star to set a 1-5 rating, but pressing Tab to it and then Enter or arrow keys does nothing. Does this pass SC 2.1.1 Keyboard?
choices: Yes, because the widget is still visible and usable with a mouse
No, because the rating functionality has no keyboard-operable equivalent
Yes, because star ratings are decorative and not required functionality
It depends on whether the widget uses a path-dependent gesture
